questions.question: The denominator of a rational number exceeds its numerator by 10. If the numerator is increased by 4 and the denominator is reduced by 3, the number obtained is (5)/(6). The original rational number is:
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

Let the numerator be x and the denominator be y,

The denominator of a rational number exceeds its numerator by 10,

⇒ y = x + 10 ----(1)

If the numerator is increased by 4 and the denominator is reduced by 3, the number obtained is 5/6,

⇒ (x + 4) / (y - 3) = 5/6

⇒ (x + 4) / (x + 10 - 3) = 5/6

⇒ (x + 4) / (x + 7) = 5/6

⇒ x = 11

⇒ y = 21

**∴ Original rational number = 11/21**

questions.question:
Primary growth in plants occurs by:

A. Vertical meristem

B. Lateral meristem

C. Intercalary meristem

D. Apical meristem
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**​C and D**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Meristem or merismatic tissue is a plant tissue that has undifferentiated cells capable of cell division and plant growth.
 
• Tissues are divided into various types such as Merismatic tissue and Permanent tissue.
 
 
• **Merismatic tissues divide throughout their lives to form new cells which differentiate to form permanent tissues.**
 
• They are rounded, oval, polygonal or rectangular without intercellular spaces.
 
• Merismatic tissue in turn classified into three types: Apical meristem, Lateral meristem and Intercalary meristem.

questions.question: The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to four times the perimeter of a square. If a quarter of the numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square, then the length of one side of the square is:
questions.solution:
Let the length of the edge of a cube be a

No of edges in a cube = 12

⇒ Length of the edges of a cube = 12a

Let the side of a square be x,

The sum of the lengths of the edges of a cube is equal to four times the perimeter of a square,

⇒ 12a = 16x

⇒ a = 4/3x

The quarter of the numerical value of the volume of the cube is equal to the numerical value of the area of the square,

⇒ 1/4a³ = x²

⇒ 1/4 × 64/27x³ = x²

∴ Side of a square, x = 27/16 units

questions.question: An element A forms an oxide with the formula A3O4. What is the valency of element A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__4__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxides are compounds that are combined with one or more oxygen atoms, for example, Carbon dioxide (CO₂), Water (H₂O), Nitrogen oxide (NO₂) etc.**
 
• Mixed oxide forms when two or more simple oxides combine and these simple oxides can be the same or different.
 
• A3O4 is an undefined mixed oxide and is a mixture of A2O3 and AO and so the element two-thirds of A has a valency of 3 and one-third has a valency of 2.
 
• Oxygen, a non-metal that has an atomic number of 8, is a 16th-group element and Lead (Pb) is a 14th-group element with an atomic number of 82.
 
 
• **The valency of oxygen is 2 and that of Lead is 4.**
 
 
 
• **Pb₃O₄ is a mixed oxide of two compounds PbO and PbO2. **The number of oxygen atoms is 4 and so the total valency is given as 8**.**
 
 
• **​**The difference between the oxygen total valency and the **Lead (Pb) valency (which is 4)** gives the** valency of the compound i.e., 8-4 = 4.** Hence option 4 is correct
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oxides are divided into different types based on valency: Simple oxides, Acidic oxides, Basic oxides and Mixed oxides.
 
• **Simple Oxides are made up of one metal** and carry only that number of oxygen atoms allowed by the normal valency of the element or metal. 
 
 
• **Examples of simple oxides include H₂O, MgO etc.**
 
 
 
• **Acidic oxide, formed by non-metals reacts with water and produces acid. For example, SO₂, CO₂ etc.**
 
• **The basic oxide reacts with water to give a base and is basic in nature, for example, Na₂O, CaO etc.**

questions.question: Pinaki is 9 years younger than Bhaswati. Thirteen years hence Bhaswati will be 1.2 times as old as Pinaki. Find Pinaki's present age.

Pinaki is 9 years younger than Bhaswati.

Concept of age

Pinaki is 9 years younger than Bhaswati,

Let Pinaki’s present age be x years

questions.question: Which part of the brain regulates breathing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Medulla**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The brain is a vital part of the Central Nervous System (CNS) and it is the anterior portion of the CNS that is located in the cranial cavity (cranium of the skull).
 
• **It consists of three parts namely Forebrain, Midbrain and Hindbrain.**
 
• Hindbrain is further distinguished into three parts Cerebellum, Medulla and Pons (located below the mid-brain and medulla in the above).
 
 
• Medulla Oblongata extends from the pons to the spinal cord.
 
• **Medulla regulates heart rate, blood pressure, breathing, swallowing, and salivation integrates signals from the spinal cord and sends the resulting signals to the Cerebrum. Hence option 4 is correct.**
 
 
 
• Cerebellum controls rapid muscular activities like running, talking etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The forebrain includes olfactory lobes (sense of smell) which are the anterior part of the brain formed by a pair of short club-shaped structures and are surrounded by the cerebral hemisphere.**
 
• Cerebrum is the largest and most complex part of the brain that parts connected by a large bundle of myelinated fibres, the corpus callosum etc.
 
 
• **The outer part of the Cerebrum is called the Cerebral cortex and the outer part is filled with grey matter and the inner part with white matter.**
 
 
 
• **Thalamus controls sensory inputs, and the body senses except for smell and is located in the middle of the brain whereas Hypothalamus controls the urge for eating and drinking.**
 
• The Midbrain is located in between the Thalamus, Hypothalamus of the forebrain and Pons of the Hindbrain and both parts form the brain stem that controls the sense of sight.

questions.question: What is the value of acceleration due to gravity on the surface of the earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9.8 m/s2**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Acceleration is due to the gravitational force and is called acceleration due to gravity and is denoted by 'g'.
 
 
• ** Its SI unit is m/s².**
 
• It is a vector quantity and its direction is towards the centre of the earth.
 
 
 
• **The value of acceleration due to gravity changes from place to place on earth, so, 9.8 m/s² (if we do not consider the resistance of air) is considered for all practical purposes. Hence option 2 is correct.**
 
• **At the centre of the earth or at the Equator, the acceleration due to gravity is '0' while its value increases when we move from the equator to the poles and becomes maximum at the poles.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Force acting on a body due to gravity is given by, F = mg, where m is the mass of the body and g is the acceleration due to gravity.
 
• **The universal law of Gravitation states that every particle attracts another particle and the force exerts is directly proportional to the product of the mass and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them**.
 
 
• It is given by F ∝ (m1m2)/(r²) and also given by F = G(m1m2)/(r²) where the **universal gravitational constant is given by 6.673 x 10⁻¹¹ N m²/kg².**

questions.question: Acids that contain Hydrogen and other non-metallic element(s), except Oxygen, are called:

• Non-metals are elements that lack metallic properties and are poor conductors of heat and electricity. 
 
 
• **They have the tendency to accept electrons and form an anion.**
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen, Helium, Carbon, Nitrogen, Fluorine etc are some examples of non-metals.**
 
• Acids are substances that are sour in taste and have one or more replaceable hydrogen atoms.
 
• **The acids that contain hydrogen and other non-metals but not oxygen are called Hydracids. Hence option 2 is correct.**

• Acids that dissociate completely when dissolved in water are called strong acids.
 
 
• **Examples of strong acids are Sulphuric acid (H₂SO₄), Hydrochloric acid (HCl), Nitric acid (HNO₃) etc.**
 
 
 
• Acids that dissociate partially when dissolved in water are called weak acids.
 
 
• **Examples include Acetic acid (CH₃COOH), Oxalic acid, Carbonic acid (H₂CO3) etc.**
 
 
 
• **In an aqueous solution, if the concentration of acid is low, then it is called dilute acid and if the concentration is high, it is called concentrated acid.**
